solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A revolutionary has months in charge of higher education

definitions.note: used attributively: to do with higher education, as in an academic post

parts.note: Jack Cade led the 1450 rebellion in Kent against Henry VI

explanation.surface: A rebel, appointed for some months, finds themselves running a university.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade was an English rebel of 1450; he is a crossword staple for 'revolutionary'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to universities and scholarly study, the world of higher education.

clue.text: Applaud actor's lines turning up in silly speech

parts.note: to applaud is to clap

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: an actor's part is the set of lines they speak

explanation.surface: An audience cheers as an actor's script appears in the middle of some nonsensical oration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses PART to TRAP beneath CLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense, empty talk designed to win applause, so foolish speech.

clue.text: One hanging around after slow lift

indicators.note: after places the waiting one behind the word for slow

parts.note: dumb can mean slow-witted
someone who hangs around is a waiter, one who waits

explanation.surface: Someone loiters around after a sluggish elevator finally arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One hanging around' reads as a loiterer in the surface; in the wordplay it is simply someone who waits, and 'slow' means slow-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbwaiter is a small hoist carrying food or dishes between floors, a kind of small elevator.

clue.text: Fishing reel using gearing that's behind the times?

definitions.meaning: an angler's reel whose gears turn the spool several times per crank of the handle
in a product such as 4 x 7, the number after the times sign, the one that multiplies

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned angler's reel, with its outdated gear mechanism, sounds hopelessly out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind the times' usually means old-fashioned; here 'times' is the multiplication sign and the number after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A geared fishing reel is called this type; in arithmetic, the number by which another is multiplied bears the same name.

clue.text: Sudden change of mind about betting odds

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
a bookmaker's price is the odds offered

explanation.surface: A punter abruptly reconsiders a wager because of the odds on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a whim, an impulsive and unpredictable shift of mood or decision.

clue.text: Stare at headless phantom

indicators.note: headless means the first letter of the word for phantom is cut off

parts.note: a bogle is a ghost or goblin, chiefly in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone gawps at a ghost that has lost its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' removes the B from BOGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to look at someone with obvious, often lecherous, interest, to gaze or leer.

clue.text: At home taking wine with uncle

definitions.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, so something with uncle has been pawned

parts.note: in means at home
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: Someone stays in, drinking wine with their uncle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncle' looks like a relative but is the old slang for the pawnbroker; HOCK is the British name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods held by a pawnbroker are pawned, and a person in debt that way is said to be pawned too.

clue.text: Make concerned university bother about society

indicators.note: about means the word for bother goes around the letter for society

parts.note: to nettle is to irritate or bother

explanation.surface: A university worries about how society is bothered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts NETTLE around S.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle someone is to disturb or worry them, making them anxious.

clue.text: Chap is no angler, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of no angler are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man laments that, sadly, he is no fisherman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges NOANGLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Algernon is a man's given name, and a male first name serves as a definition by example for a fellow.

clue.text: Creature with a male mother discovered in 1050

indicators.note: discovered in means these letters are found inside the Roman numerals

parts.note: in Roman numerals M is 1000 and L is 50
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A strange animal with a male parent is found in the eleventh century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered in' puts AMMA inside ML, the Roman numerals for 1050.
explanation.definitionFit: A mammal is one kind of animal, so this is a definition by example of a living being.

clue.text: HRE 60

parts.note: the clue's three letters are the inner part, the core, of the word for the number after two

explanation.walkthrough: HRE is the heart of THREE, so it is THREE'S CORE; run together that reads THREESCORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so three of them make sixty, the old way of counting in twenties.

clue.text: Piece of ground needs a proper cut

indicators.note: cut means the word for proper has its last letter chopped off

parts.note: real means proper or genuine

explanation.surface: A plot of land requires a decent mowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the L from REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or stretch of land, a section of terrain.

clue.text: Thief making moves to kick cop in peevish fit

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the word for peevish fit

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking or bad temper

indicators.note: making moves suggests the letters of kick cop shift about into a new order

explanation.surface: A criminal moves to kick a policeman during a tantrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making moves' is the anagram signal on 'kick cop'; 'peevish fit' is an old sense of pet, a sulk, and 'in' splits it around the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickpocket is a thief who steals from people's pockets or bags.

clue.text: Commission penny with the Queen — another coin with date

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth
a cent is a coin, another besides the penny
an age is a period or era, a date in history

explanation.surface: Commission is paid in pennies, with the Queen's head on coins bearing a date.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A commission is a fee calculated as a proportion of a sale, so a percentage cut.

clue.text: Be a companion to old parliamentarian Liberal in fix?

indicators.note: in means these letters sit inside the word for fix

parts.note: to cement is to fix firmly
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An elderly Liberal MP in trouble is offered company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fix' looks like a predicament but is the verb CEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To complement something is to go well with it, completing it as a partner does.

clue.text: Family having rams brought over in pioneer vehicle

indicators.note: brought over means the combined letters are turned round

parts.note: kin are family
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A family brings its sheep across in an early farm wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' reverses KINTUPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputnik 1 was the first artificial satellite, launched in 1957, a trailblazing spacecraft.

clue.text: So my acer turned out to be an American plane

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters of so my acer are turned over into a different order

explanation.surface: A gardener finds their maple tree is really a US species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges SOMYACER. 'plane' looks like an aircraft but is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America the plane tree Platanus occidentalis is called by this name, though in Britain it means a maple.

clue.text: Clubs fight in the US and break up

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
rumble is American slang for a street fight between gangs

explanation.surface: American nightclubs see brawls and fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumble is to fall into small fragments, to disintegrate.

clue.text: Italian turns up in frightful uncool expression

indicators.note: in means the reversed letters go inside the jumbled ones
frightful suggests something dreadful, so the letters of uncool are jumbled
in a down clue, turns up means the letters for Italian are read bottom to top, so backwards

explanation.surface: An Italian shows up in some dreadfully unfashionable phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightful' signals the anagram of 'uncool'; 'turns up' reverses the abbreviation, since this is a down light, and 'in' places the result within the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A locution is a word or phrase, particularly a characteristic way of saying something.

clue.text: Abnormally hungry but limit must go short on calories initially

indicators.note: go short means each of the two words loses its last letter
initially means the first letter of calories is taken

explanation.surface: Someone ravenous is told to cut back and limit their calories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must go short' trims both 'but' and 'limit', leaving BU and LIMI.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulimia is an eating disorder marked by bouts of insatiable appetite, so the adjective means pathologically ravenous.

clue.text: Plan recycling for green alcohol

parts.note: a chart is a map or plan
to recycle something is to reuse it

explanation.surface: A scheme for recycling helps an environmentally friendly drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks ecological but is the liqueur's colour; 'recycling' is a synonym, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a French herbal liqueur, famously green (also yellow), made by Carthusian monks.

clue.text: Screen beginning to cut out vitamin from sunlight

indicators.note: to cut out means the letter for the vitamin is removed from the word for beginning

parts.note: a dawning is a beginning or first appearance
vitamin D is made by the skin in sunlight

explanation.surface: Something that blocks the sun's rays starts to remove a vitamin from them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen ... from sunlight' wants to be the definition, but 'from sunlight' belongs to the vitamin: D is the sunshine vitamin.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canopy stretched over a window or doorway to shade it, a kind of shelter.

clue.text: Negligent missing son's absence

indicators.note: missing means the word for negligent goes without the letter for son

parts.note: slack means careless or negligent
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A careless parent fails to notice their son is gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops the S from SLACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack is a want or deficiency, the state of something not being there.

clue.text: One who believes some number to be involved in disputed robbery

indicators.note: to be involved in means the letter goes inside the following words

parts.note: moot means open to debate
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics
a heist is a robbery

explanation.surface: A believer is caught up in an argument over a theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be involved in' puts N into MOOTHEIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A monotheist believes in a single God, so is one kind of religious believer; the definition is deliberately vague.

clue.text: Prepare for cutting hospital unit

parts.note: one is the unit number

explanation.surface: A hospital ward gets ready for surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' suggests surgery but means sharpening a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: To hone a blade is to sharpen it on a whetstone so that it will slice well.

clue.text: Super nervous reaction coming from vinegar

parts.note: ace means excellent, super
a tic is an involuntary nervous twitch

explanation.surface: An excellent twitch is brought on by tasting vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetic acid is the main constituent of vinegar, so the adjective means derived from or relating to it.

clue.text: Rupees I'm circulating with Benin currency

indicators.note: circulating, as money does, suggests these letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: Rupees and other cash circulate in the West African country of Benin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' rearranges R, IM and BENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The renminbi is the official money of the People's Republic of China.

clue.text: Acting dishonestly about effect of global warming

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
global warming heats the planet, so its effect is heating

explanation.surface: A scientist fudges the data on climate change.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating means behaving deceitfully to gain an advantage.
